questionsAcceptableUse.question: An employee wants to use their USC email and cloud storage to help run a small side business they own, only during their unpaid lunch break. Is this acceptable under the policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, as long as it's limited to unpaid break time.

options.label: B
options.text: No — personal use must not be associated with any for-profit outside business activity, regardless of timing.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, if their manager gives verbal approval.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, as long as it's under 30 minutes per day.

questionsAcceptableUse.explanation: Section 3.1 states personal use must not be associated with any for-profit outside business activity. The fact that the activity occurs during unpaid break time does not change that restriction.

questionsAcceptableUse.question: A colleague is locked out of their own account and asks to use your login just this once to finish an urgent task. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Share your credentials since it's a one-time favour for a colleague.

options.label: B
options.text: Share your credentials, then change your password afterward.

options.label: C
options.text: Decline — employees must use only their own log-on ID and password, and credentials must not be shared.

options.label: D
options.text: Share your credentials only if you stay logged in to supervise.

questionsAcceptableUse.explanation: Section 4.2 requires personnel to use their own log-on ID and password only, and prohibits sharing credentials.

questionsAcceptableUse.question: Your work laptop has been running slowly, and you suspect the antivirus software is the cause. What does the policy require?

options.label: A
options.text: You may disable it temporarily and re-enable it the same day.

options.label: B
options.text: You must not disable antivirus software; report the issue instead.

options.label: C
options.text: You may disable it outside of business hours.

options.label: D
options.text: You may disable it if you notify a coworker first.

questionsAcceptableUse.explanation: Section 4.1 states users must not disable antivirus software and should report virus occurrences or related issues.

questionsAcceptableUse.question: After a frustrating call with a vendor, an employee sends a profanity-laced, angry email about them using the corporate email system. Which part of the policy does this violate?

options.label: A
options.text: Section 3, Personal Use.

options.label: B
options.text: Section 2, Corporate Public Image, which prohibits abusive or profane communications through corporate systems.

options.label: C
options.text: Section 6, Data Protection.

options.label: D
options.text: Section 7, Working From Home.

questionsAcceptableUse.explanation: Section 2.1 prohibits abusive, discriminatory, harassing, inflammatory, profane, or offensive communications on corporate systems.

questionsAcceptableUse.question: An employee is working from home on their personal laptop and needs to store USC member files locally to complete a project. What must be true of that laptop under the policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Nothing additional is required, since it is the employee's own device.

options.label: B
options.text: It must be patched to the latest secure version, run up-to-date security software, and be password protected.

options.label: C
options.text: The files must be printed rather than stored digitally.

options.label: D
options.text: It only needs COO approval to be used this way.

questionsAcceptableUse.explanation: Section 7.1 requires personal devices accessing USC data to be patched, running current security software, and password protected.

questionsCustomerService.question: A customer with a disability wants to bring their service animal into a USC public-facing space. What is the USC's approach?

options.label: A
options.text: Service animals are never permitted indoors.

options.label: B
options.text: The USC welcomes service animals onto premises open to the public, and commits to finding alternatives where animals are legally prohibited.

options.label: C
options.text: Only guide dogs are permitted; no other service animals.

options.label: D
options.text: A written doctor's note is required at every visit.

questionsCustomerService.explanation: Section 4.2.1 states the USC welcomes persons with disabilities accompanied by a service animal onto premises open to the public, and commits to finding alternatives if service animals are prohibited by law.

questionsCustomerService.question: The USC needs to temporarily close an accessible entrance for repairs. What must it do?

options.label: A
options.text: Wait until the repair is finished before announcing anything.

options.label: B
options.text: Nothing, as long as repairs are completed quickly.

options.label: C
options.text: Notify customers promptly with a clearly posted notice including the reason, anticipated length, and available alternatives.

options.label: D
options.text: Only inform USC staff, not the public.

questionsCustomerService.explanation: Section 4.4.1 requires prompt notification of service disruptions via a clearly posted notice including the reason, anticipated length, and alternatives, if available.

questionsCustomerService.question: A support person accompanies a customer with a disability into a paid event. If a fee applies to the support person, what must the USC do?

options.label: A
options.text: Charge the support person double the standard fee.

options.label: B
options.text: It is never permitted to charge a fee for a support person.

options.label: C
options.text: Always waive the fee automatically.

options.label: D
options.text: Communicate and post the fee accordingly through the USC's website, brochure, or other public methods.

questionsCustomerService.explanation: Section 4.3.2 states that where a fee applies to a support person's admission, it will be communicated and posted through the USC's website, brochure, or other public methods.

questionsCustomerService.question: When must training on this policy be provided to a new employee who deals with the public?

options.label: A
options.text: As soon as practicable after being assigned applicable duties.

options.label: B
options.text: Within their first year, at any point.

options.label: C
options.text: Only during annual refresher sessions.

options.label: D
options.text: Only if the employee requests it.

questionsCustomerService.explanation: Section 4.5.3 states training will be provided to each person as soon as practicable after being assigned applicable duties.

questionsCustomerService.question: A customer wants to provide feedback about their accessibility experience with the USC. How can this be submitted?

options.label: A
options.text: Only by mail.

options.label: B
options.text: In person, by telephone, in writing, or electronically via email or other digital formats.

options.label: C
options.text: Only through a third-party ombudsperson.

options.label: D
options.text: Feedback is not accepted from the general public.

questionsCustomerService.explanation: Section 4.6.1 states feedback can be given in person, by telephone, in writing, or electronically via email or other digital formats.

questionsAccessibility.question: An applicant is selected to participate in an interview process. What must the USC do regarding accommodations?

options.label: A
options.text: Accommodations are only discussed after the applicant's first 90 days of employment.

options.label: B
options.text: Nothing, unless the applicant is ultimately hired.

options.label: C
options.text: Notify the applicant that accommodations are available upon request, and consult with them to provide or arrange suitable accommodation.

options.label: D
options.text: Only offer accommodations after a formal complaint is filed.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.11.1 states the USC notifies job applicants selected for an assessment or selection process that accommodations are available upon request, and consults with and provides or arranges suitable accommodation.

questionsAccessibility.question: A customer's service animal isn't easily identifiable by a harness or vest, and staff need to confirm it's required for a disability. What can staff request?

options.label: A
options.text: A government-issued identification card for the animal.

options.label: B
options.text: Proof of veterinary vaccination only.

options.label: C
options.text: Nothing — staff may never ask for confirmation.

options.label: D
options.text: Documentation from a regulated health professional confirming the person needs the service animal for reasons relating to their disability.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.4.2 states staff may ask for documentation from a regulated health professional when a service animal cannot be easily identified.

questionsAccessibility.question: The USC is redesigning a service counter in a public space. What minimum clear knee space must it provide from the public-facing side, per this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: 750 mm wide x 680 mm high x 250 mm deep, with additional toe space beyond.

options.label: B
options.text: 1000 mm wide x 800 mm high x 300 mm deep.

options.label: C
options.text: No specific dimensions are required.

options.label: D
options.text: 500 mm wide x 500 mm high x 200 mm deep.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.12.3.1.a specifies clear knee space of 750 mm wide x 680 mm high x 250 mm deep below the service counter, with additional toe space of 750 mm wide x 230 mm high x 230 mm deep.

questionsAccessibility.question: An employee with a disability needs individualized workplace emergency information. When will the USC review this information?

options.label: A
options.text: Only once, when the employee is first hired.

options.label: B
options.text: When the employee changes location, when their accommodation needs or plans are reviewed, or when the employer reviews its general emergency response policies.

options.label: C
options.text: Only if requested in writing on an annual basis.

options.label: D
options.text: Never — this is handled entirely by the employee.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.11.7 lists these three triggers for reviewing individualized workplace emergency response information.

questionsAccessibility.question: A person with a disability requests an accessible format of a USC document. What cost, if any, can be charged?

options.label: A
options.text: A cost determined case-by-case with no cap.

options.label: B
options.text: A standard administrative fee.

options.label: C
options.text: No additional cost — the format will be provided at no additional cost and in a timely manner.

options.label: D
options.text: A cost equal to printing and shipping expenses.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.8.2 states the USC will provide accessible formats or communication supports at no additional cost and in a timely manner.

questionsAccessibility.question: If an assistive device presents a significant and unavoidable health or safety concern, what does the USC commit to doing?

options.label: A
options.text: Requiring a liability waiver with no further accommodation.

options.label: B
options.text: Charging an additional insurance fee.

options.label: C
options.text: Prohibiting the person with a disability from accessing the premises.

options.label: D
options.text: Using other measures to ensure the person with a disability can still access goods, services, or facilities.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.2.2 states that where an assistive device presents a significant and unavoidable health or safety concern, other measures will be used to ensure access.

questionsAccessibility.question: Before requiring a support person for health or safety reasons, what must the USC do first?

options.label: A
options.text: Consult with the person with a disability, consider available evidence, and determine there is no other reasonable way to protect health or safety.

options.label: B
options.text: Only obtain approval from the Senior Manager, Communications.

options.label: C
options.text: Post a general public notice, with no individual consultation required.

options.label: D
options.text: Nothing — it can require a support person unilaterally.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.5.5 requires consultation with the person with a disability, consideration of available evidence, and confirmation that no other reasonable option exists before making this decision.

questionsAccessibility.question: What accessibility standard must USC websites meet under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: WCAG 1.0 Level A.

options.label: B
options.text: WCAG 2.0 Level AA.

options.label: C
options.text: WCAG 2.1 Level AAA.

options.label: D
options.text: No specific standard is required.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.10.5 states the USC will meet internationally-recognized WCAG 2.0 Level AA website requirements.

questionsConflict.question: An employee paid through honoraria wants to take on a second, separate paid USC staff role at the same time. Is this permitted?

options.label: A
options.text: No — paid employees, including those paid through honoraria, may hold only one USC position at a time.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, with only verbal manager approval.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, as long as combined hours stay under 40 per week.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, as long as the two roles don't overlap in duties.

questionsConflict.explanation: Section 5.1 states paid employees, including those paid through honoraria, shall hold one position with the USC at a time.

questionsConflict.question: A paid staff member wants to run for USC Councillor while continuing in their current paid role. What does the policy say?

options.label: A
options.text: It's permitted since Councillor is an elected, not paid, position.

options.label: B
options.text: Paid employees may not apply or run for Councillor while holding their paid position.

options.label: C
options.text: It's permitted only with Board of Directors approval.

options.label: D
options.text: It's permitted after six months in the paid role.

questionsConflict.explanation: Section 5.3 prohibits certain paid staff from applying or running for USC Councillor (and other listed positions) while they hold their paid position.

questionsConflict.question: A paid employee applies for a hired executive position with the USC. Must they take an unpaid leave of absence during the process?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, for at least two weeks.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, for the duration of the hiring process.

options.label: C
options.text: No — this is treated as an internal hiring process and no leave is required.

options.label: D
options.text: Only if they currently hold a Director role.

questionsConflict.explanation: Section 5.4 states paid employees applying for a hired executive position will not be required to take a leave of absence, as it is treated as an internal hiring process.

questionsConflict.question: A department wants to consult on filling a USC elected student leadership position and isn't sure who to go through. Per the policy, who should this consultation go through?

options.label: A
options.text: The Senior Manager, Information Systems.

options.label: B
options.text: The Human Resources Committee only.

options.label: C
options.text: The Board of Directors directly.

options.label: D
options.text: The President and Vice-Presidents.

questionsConflict.explanation: Section 5.6 states consultations for USC hired and elected student leadership positions shall go through the President and Vice-Presidents.

questionsDisc.question: An employee overhears a coworker repeatedly making unwelcome comments about another colleague's ethnic origin. What does this policy expect of the employee who overheard it?

options.label: A
options.text: To report it to their Manager/Supervisor and not willfully ignore a poisoned environment.

options.label: B
options.text: To wait and see if the targeted coworker files a complaint first.

options.label: C
options.text: To handle it informally themselves and not report it further.

options.label: D
options.text: Nothing, since they weren't the target of the comments.

questionsDisc.explanation: Sections 5.2.5 and 5.2.8 require Members not to willfully ignore a poisoned environment and to report incidents of discrimination or harassment to their Manager/Supervisor.

questionsDisc.question: A Member witnesses an immediate, escalating threat of violence in the workplace right now. What is the correct first step?

options.label: A
options.text: Document the incident and raise it at the next staff meeting.

options.label: B
options.text: Contact Campus Police at 911 (or ext. 83300) immediately, given the immediate danger.

options.label: C
options.text: Wait until the person involved calms down before reporting.

options.label: D
options.text: Email the Senior Manager, People and Development and wait for a reply.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 5.2.9 directs individuals to contact Campus Police at 911 or ext. 83300 in the event of an emergency or threat of violence.

questionsDisc.question: Does this policy apply to general student-to-student conduct within Western University?

options.label: A
options.text: Only if a USC Member is also directly involved.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, in all circumstances.

options.label: C
options.text: No — it is not intended to apply to general student-to-student or student-to-University contact.

options.label: D
options.text: Only during Orientation Week.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 1.3 states the Policy is not intended to be applied to general student-to-student or student-to-University contact within Western University.

questionsDisc.question: An anonymous but credible report suggests harassment may be occurring, though no formal complaint has been filed. What is the USC's obligation?

options.label: A
options.text: The matter can only be raised by the alleged victim.

options.label: B
options.text: The report must be dismissed as unverifiable.

options.label: C
options.text: No action is required without a formal, signed complaint.

options.label: D
options.text: The USC shall investigate reports or incidents of harassment, discrimination, or violence even without a formal complaint.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 4.3 states the USC shall investigate reports or incidents of harassment, discrimination, or violence even if no formal complaint has been made.

questionsDisc.question: Who administers this policy if the Senior Manager, People and Development is personally conflicted, such as being named in a complaint?

options.label: A
options.text: The Chief Operating Officer.

options.label: B
options.text: Any available Board member.

options.label: C
options.text: The chair of the Human Resources Committee.

options.label: D
options.text: The complainant's direct supervisor.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 3.1 states the Chief Operating Officer shall be responsible for administering the Policy if the Senior Manager, People and Development is involved in a complaint.

questionsDisc.question: Which of the following best matches the policy's definition of a 'poisoned environment'?

options.label: A
options.text: A single minor disagreement between coworkers.

options.label: B
options.text: A workplace where harassment or discrimination is so severe or frequent it creates an intimidating or hostile environment affecting work or academic performance.

options.label: C
options.text: Any workplace experiencing high stress or workload.

options.label: D
options.text: A workplace with inadequate physical facilities.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 2.4 defines a poisoned environment as one where harassment or discrimination is so severe or frequent that it creates an intimidating or hostile environment.

questionsDisc.question: A Member wants to know whether this policy's definition of harassment covers messages sent by text or instant message rather than in person. Is virtual conduct covered?

options.label: A
options.text: Only if the recipient forwards it to a supervisor within 24 hours.

options.label: B
options.text: No, only in-person conduct is covered.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes — the definition of harassment specifically includes virtual communication incidents.

options.label: D
options.text: Only if the message is sent during scheduled work hours.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 2.2 states harassment includes virtual communication incidents.

questionsEarly.question: An employee's absence due to a work-related injury is expected to last only three days. Who is responsible for maintaining communication with them during this time?

options.label: A
options.text: The Senior Manager, People and Development, on a weekly basis.

options.label: B
options.text: The employee's supervisor.

options.label: C
options.text: The WSIB case manager directly.

options.label: D
options.text: The Joint Health and Safety Committee.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 4.1.9 states that where an absence is expected to be short-term (not exceeding five days), communication is maintained through the employee's supervisor.

questionsEarly.question: An employee's absence is now expected to exceed five days. Who takes over handling communications on behalf of the USC?

options.label: A
options.text: The employee's supervisor continues to handle it alone.

options.label: B
options.text: The Senior Manager, People and Development.

options.label: C
options.text: The Union.

options.label: D
options.text: WSIB directly.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 4.1.9 states that if an absence exceeds or is expected to exceed five days, the Senior Manager, People and Development shall handle communications on behalf of the USC.

questionsEarly.question: An investigation determines that an employee's injury claim was fraudulent. What is the consequence under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: A verbal warning only, regardless of severity.

options.label: B
options.text: Progressive discipline up to and including termination, and immediate reporting to WSIB.

options.label: C
options.text: No formal consequence unless it happens more than once.

options.label: D
options.text: The employee is simply removed from the return to work program with no further action.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 1.3 states a claim deemed fraudulent will result in progressive discipline up to and including termination, and will be reported to WSIB immediately.

questionsEarly.question: An employer wants to offer an employee 'suitable work' as part of a return to work plan. Which of the following is NOT one of the required characteristics of suitable work under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: It is available and can be started quickly.

options.label: B
options.text: It requires entirely new skills unrelated to the employee's existing abilities.

options.label: C
options.text: It is safe and within the employee's physical capabilities.

options.label: D
options.text: It restores pre-injury/illness earnings as much as reasonably possible.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 5.1.1 defines suitable work as available and quick to start, safe and within physical capabilities, using skills the employee has or can attain, and restoring earnings — not requiring entirely unrelated new skills.

questionsEarly.question: An employee sustains a work-related injury and is later declared fit to return to work in some capacity. At the latest, until what point must the USC continue making every effort to find suitable work?

options.label: A
options.text: Six months after the injury occurred.

options.label: B
options.text: The earlier of 12 months after being declared fit to return, or 24 months after the date of the injury/illness.

options.label: C
options.text: Indefinitely, with no time limit.

options.label: D
options.text: Only until the end of the calendar year in which the injury occurred.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 5.2.1 states the USC will make every effort to find suitable work up until the earlier of 12 months after being declared fit to return, or 24 months after the injury/illness date (among other listed end points).

questionsEarly.question: An employee disagrees with how the USC has handled their return to work plan and wants to raise a dispute. What is the first step under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: File a complaint directly with WSIB.

options.label: B
options.text: Direct the dispute initially to the Chief Operating Officer.

options.label: C
options.text: Resign and reapply for the position.

options.label: D
options.text: Contact the Joint Health and Safety Committee directly.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 6.1 states disputes regarding the fulfillment of this policy may initially be directed to the Chief Operating Officer.

questionsEarly.question: A worker on modified duties is asked by the employer to attend an independent medical assessment. What is expected of the employee?

options.label: A
options.text: They may decline, since the request came from the employer rather than their own treating doctor.

options.label: B
options.text: They must comply with the recommendations of treating healthcare professionals and attend independent assessments as requested.

options.label: C
options.text: Only unionized employees are required to attend such assessments.

options.label: D
options.text: They may attend only if compensated separately for their time.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 3.2.6 requires employees to comply with recommendations of treating healthcare professionals and attend independent assessments as requested.

questionsEmergency.question: A fire breaks out in a USC office. What is the correct first action per the procedures referenced in this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Use the elevator to leave the building quickly.

options.label: B
options.text: Wait for a building-wide announcement before moving.

options.label: C
options.text: Call ext. 83304 before doing anything else.

options.label: D
options.text: Raise the alarm from a safe area on the way to evacuate, then use stairwells.

questionsEmergency.explanation: Section 4.1.1 directs raising the alarm from a safe area on the way to evacuate the building and using stairwells to evacuate.

questionsEmergency.question: An employee needs to report a suspected gas leak. Which number should they call?

options.label: A
options.text: 911 - Western Campus Police.

questionsEmergency.explanation: Section 3.1.2.7 lists gas leaks (among other emergencies) as reportable to 911 - Western Campus Police.

questionsEmergency.question: Who has the authority within the USC to declare an emergency and close regular operations?

options.label: A
options.text: Any employee who feels unsafe.

options.label: B
options.text: The USC Emergency Response Representative.

options.label: C
options.text: The Health & Safety Coordinator only.

options.label: D
options.text: Western Campus Police exclusively.

questionsEmergency.explanation: Section 3.2.1 states the USC Emergency Response Representative has authority within the USC to declare an emergency and close regular operations.

questionsEmergency.question: An employee cannot safely evacuate during a situation of immediate danger. What should they do?

options.label: A
options.text: Exit through a window if on a low floor.

options.label: B
options.text: Attempt to move through the danger to reach the nearest stairwell.

options.label: C
options.text: Seek shelter where they are, lock doors, avoid windows, and call Campus Police at 911.

options.label: D
options.text: Wait by the elevator for rescue.

questionsEmergency.explanation: Section 4.2.3 directs seeking shelter where you are if safe evacuation is not possible, locking doors, avoiding windows, and calling Campus Police at 911.

questionsEmergency.question: A visitor becomes seriously injured and requires emergency transport to a medical facility. Who is permitted to provide this transport?

options.label: A
options.text: The visitor's own emergency contact.

options.label: B
options.text: Any campus security staff, regardless of medical training.

options.label: C
options.text: Any nearby employee with a vehicle.

options.label: D
options.text: Only personnel trained and acting within their competency.

questionsEmergency.explanation: Section 4.3 states persons requiring emergency transportation to a medical facility must be transferred by trained personnel acting within their competency.

questionsHazard.question: A worker notices a loose stairwell handrail that poses a real risk of injury but cannot fix it themselves. What should they do?

options.label: A
options.text: Report the hazard to their supervisor/manager immediately and verbally, using the Hazard Reporting Form if it is significant.

options.label: B
options.text: Wait until the next scheduled inspection to mention it.

options.label: C
options.text: Post a handwritten note near the handrail and move on.

options.label: D
options.text: Ignore it, since it isn't part of their job.

questionsHazard.explanation: Sections 3.1 and 4.1 require workers to report significant hazards to their supervisor/manager immediately and verbally, using the Hazard Reporting Form where appropriate.

questionsHazard.question: A worker personally tightens a loose cable that was creating a trip hazard. What is required afterward?

options.label: A
options.text: Nothing further, since the hazard was already fixed.

options.label: B
options.text: Report both the hazard and the remedy made to their supervisor/manager.

options.label: C
options.text: Only report it if someone was actually injured.

options.label: D
options.text: File a formal report directly with the Board of Directors.

questionsHazard.explanation: Section 3.2 states a worker who remedies a significant hazard will report both the hazard and the remedy made to their supervisor/manager.

questionsHazard.question: Who is responsible for ensuring the Health & Safety Coordinator receives copies of a hazard report for distribution to the JHSC and Worker Health & Safety Representative?

options.label: A
options.text: USC Occupational Health & Safety only.

options.label: B
options.text: The worker who first identified the hazard.

options.label: C
options.text: The supervisor/manager of the worker reporting the hazard.

options.label: D
options.text: The Board of Directors.

questionsHazard.explanation: Section 3.4 places responsibility on the supervisor/manager of the reporting worker to ensure the Health & Safety Coordinator receives copies for distribution.

questionsHazard.question: An employee cannot safely evacuate during a situation of immediate danger. What should they do?

options.label: A
options.text: Any hazard that has been reported more than once.

options.label: B
options.text: A hazard identified only during an annual inspection.

options.label: C
options.text: A minor cosmetic issue with no safety impact.

options.label: D
options.text: A condition, activity, or situation posing a considerable risk of injury, illness, death, or harm.

questionsHazard.explanation: Section 2.3 defines a serious hazard as a condition, activity, or situation that poses a considerable risk of injury, illness, death, or harm to individuals.

questionsHsrm.question: A Supervisor is unsure which section of the Occupational Health and Safety Act they are specifically responsible for under this policy. Which section applies to Supervisors?

options.label: A
options.text: Section 27.

options.label: B
options.text: Section 28.

options.label: C
options.text: Section 25.

options.label: D
options.text: Section 26.

questionsHsrm.explanation: Section 2.3 states Supervisors are responsible for section 27 of the OHSA.

questionsHsrm.question: How often are Manager and Supervisor health and safety performance evaluations performed, and in what format?

options.label: A
options.text: Once a year, quantitative only.

options.label: B
options.text: Twice a year — a midyear qualitative evaluation and a final quantitative evaluation.

options.label: C
options.text: Quarterly, qualitative only.

options.label: D
options.text: Only when requested by Human Resources.

questionsHsrm.explanation: Section 2.4.1 states performance evaluations will be performed twice each year, with a midyear qualitative and a final quantitative evaluation.

questionsHsrm.question: Who is responsible for ensuring the Health & Safety Coordinator receives copies of a hazard report for distribution to the JHSC and Worker Health & Safety Representative?

options.label: A
options.text: Referral directly to Western Campus Police.

options.label: B
options.text: Immediate termination with no process.

options.label: C
options.text: Article 12 of the collective agreement between the USC and CUPE Local 2820.

options.label: D
options.text: A verbal warning only, with no further escalation possible.

questionsHsrm.explanation: Section 3.1 states disciplinary procedures will follow the process described in Article 12 of the collective agreement between the USC and CUPE Local 2820.

questionsHsrm.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a core Manager/Supervisor responsibility under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Commending employee health and safety performance.

options.label: B
options.text: Conducting incident investigations.

options.label: C
options.text: Appointing competent supervision.

options.label: D
options.text: Personally administering all first aid treatment on-site.

questionsHsrm.explanation: Section 2.1 lists seven specific responsibilities (inspections, information sessions, incident investigations, training, correcting substandard conditions, commending performance, and appointing competent supervision) — personally administering first aid is not among them.

questionsHsrw.question: Which section of the Occupational Health and Safety Act are workers specifically responsible for under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Section 28.

options.label: B
options.text: Section 30.

options.label: C
options.text: Section 25.

options.label: D
options.text: Section 27.

questionsHsrw.explanation: Section 2.2 states workers are responsible for section 28 of the OHSA.

questionsHsrw.question: A worker repeatedly violates a known safety rule. How is this addressed under the policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Immediate termination with no warning.

options.label: B
options.text: Progressive discipline, as per Article 12 of the USC/CUPE Local 2820 collective agreement.

options.label: C
options.text: A fine deducted directly from their pay.

options.label: D
options.text: Reassignment with no formal process.

questionsHsrw.explanation: Section 3.1 states violations will be disciplined progressively as per Article 12 of the collective agreement between the USC and CUPE Local 2820.

questionsHsrw.question: Who is responsible for ensuring the Health & Safety Coordinator receives copies of a hazard report for distribution to the JHSC and Worker Health & Safety Representative?

options.label: A
options.text: Only to Managers and Supervisors.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, only direct employees.

options.label: C
options.text: No — it applies to all USC workers, including supplied labour.

options.label: D
options.text: Only to unionized staff.

questionsHsrw.explanation: Section 1.1 states this policy applies to all USC workers, and the title itself specifies it includes supplied labour.

questionsHswrp.question: A worker believes a piece of equipment is unsafe to operate and refuses to use it. What is the correct Stage 1 action?

options.label: A
options.text: Attempt to fix the equipment themselves before reporting anything.

options.label: B
options.text: Wait until their next shift to mention it.

options.label: C
options.text: Immediately leave for the day without reporting it.

options.label: D
options.text: Report the concern (preferably in writing) to their Supervisor, remain in a safe place near their workstation, and have the Supervisor investigate with the worker present.

questionsHswrp.explanation: Section 2.2.2.1 describes Stage 1 as reporting to the Supervisor (preferably in writing), remaining in a safe place, and the Supervisor investigating with the worker present.

questionsHswrp.question: After a Stage 1 investigation, a worker still has reasonable grounds to believe the work is unsafe. What happens next?

options.label: A
options.text: The worker remains in a safe place and the Ministry of Labour is notified.

options.label: B
options.text: The worker is permanently reassigned with no further process.

options.label: C
options.text: The matter is automatically dropped.

options.label: D
options.text: The worker must return to the task regardless of their concerns.

questionsHswrp.explanation: Section 2.2.2.2.a describes Stage 2, where the worker remains in a safe place and the Ministry of Labour is notified.

questionsHswrp.question: If refused work is offered to another worker during a Stage 2 review, what must happen?

options.label: A
options.text: It can be offered without informing the second worker of anything.

options.label: B
options.text: It must be offered in the presence of a JHSC worker representative and the Senior Manager, People and Development, and the second worker must be told of the original refusal and its reasons.

options.label: C
options.text: Only a manager needs to be present, with no worker representative required.

options.label: D
options.text: It can only be offered after the Ministry of Labour issues its decision.

questionsHswrp.explanation: Section 2.2.2.2.b requires refused work to be offered in the presence of a JHSC worker representative and the Senior Manager, People and Development, with the other worker advised of the refusal and reasons.

questionsHswrp.question: An employer disciplines a worker specifically because they exercised their right to refuse unsafe work. What does the policy say about this?

options.label: A
options.text: This is only prohibited for unionized staff.

options.label: B
options.text: This is permitted if handled discreetly.

options.label: C
options.text: This is a prohibited reprisal under the Occupational Health and Safety Act.

options.label: D
options.text: This is permitted if the refusal is later found to be unfounded.

questionsHswrp.explanation: Sections 3.1 and 3.2 state that reprisals such as discipline against a worker for invoking their right to refuse unsafe work are prohibited under the Occupational Health and Safety Act.

questionsHswrp.question: What grounds does the policy identify as valid reasons a worker may refuse work?

options.label: A
options.text: Personal scheduling conflicts.

options.label: B
options.text: Only unsafe physical workplace conditions.

options.label: C
options.text: Only workplace violence.

options.label: D
options.text: Unsafe equipment/machines/devices, physical workplace conditions, workplace violence, or a contravention of the Act/Regulations that may endanger a worker.

questionsHswrp.explanation: Section 2.2.1 lists these four grounds for a valid work refusal under the Occupational Health & Safety Act.

questionsHousekeeping.question: An employee's shelves and light fixtures have accumulated dust that a vacuum can't fully remove. What does the policy recommend?

options.label: A
options.text: These may require manual cleaning.

options.label: B
options.text: Leave it until the next scheduled deep clean.

options.label: C
options.text: Contact the Board of Directors directly.

options.label: D
options.text: Use compressed air to blow it off quickly.

questionsHousekeeping.explanation: Section 4.1.2 notes that dust and grime collecting on shelves, fixtures, and similar surfaces may require manual cleaning.

questionsHousekeeping.question: Which of the following is explicitly prohibited for removing dust, dirt, or chips from equipment or work surfaces?

options.label: A
options.text: Dampening floors before sweeping.

options.label: B
options.text: Compressed air.

options.label: C
options.text: Manual cleaning.

options.label: D
options.text: Vacuum cleaners.

questionsHousekeeping.explanation: Section 4.1.3 states compressed air should not be used for removing dust, dirt, or chips from equipment or work surfaces.

questionsHousekeeping.question: An employee stores personal food in the shared staff fridge for several weeks. Is this consistent with policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Only frozen items may be stored long-term.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, as long as it's labeled.

options.label: C
options.text: No — the fridge is intended for short-term food storage purposes only.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, if it's kept in a sealed container.

questionsHousekeeping.explanation: Section 2.2.2.2.b requires refused work to be offered in the presence of a JHSC worker representative and the Senior Manager, People and Development, with the other worker advised of the refusal and reasons.

questionsHousekeeping.question: Materials are being stored directly under a sprinkler head in a storage area. What clearance does the policy require?

options.label: A
options.text: At least 5 feet.

options.label: B
options.text: No clearance is required.

options.label: C
options.text: At least 6 inches.

options.label: D
options.text: At least one meter (about three feet) of clear space.

questionsHousekeeping.explanation: Section 4.9.1 states stored materials should allow at least one meter (or about three feet) of clear space under sprinkler heads.

questionsHousekeeping.question: An employee notices dim lighting in their work area due to dirty fixtures and burnt-out bulbs. What should they do?

options.label: A
options.text: Contact Manager, InfoSource and Building Services so the Physical Plant Department can be notified.

options.label: B
options.text: Ignore it, since it's a minor issue.

options.label: C
options.text: File a Hazard Reporting Form only if someone is injured.

options.label: D
options.text: Replace the bulbs themselves without reporting it.

questionsHousekeeping.explanation: Section 4.4.1 directs employees to contact Manager, InfoSource and Building Services for dirty fixtures, burnt-out bulbs, or missing lighting covers.

questionsInjury.question: An employee suffers a minor cut requiring only a bandage. Does this need to be reported under the policy?

options.label: A
options.text: No, only lost-time injuries need to be reported.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes — the policy applies to all injuries and illnesses regardless of nature or severity, including first aid cases.

options.label: C
options.text: Only if it happened during a shift longer than 8 hours.

options.label: D
options.text: Only if a supervisor happens to see it occur.

questionsInjury.explanation: Section 1.2 states this policy applies to all injuries and illnesses regardless of nature or severity, including first aid cases.

questionsInjury.question: A worker becomes unable to report their own injury due to its severity. What is required?

options.label: A
options.text: DThe First Aid provider must personally witness the injury occurring.

options.label: B
options.text: No report is made until the worker recovers enough to report it themselves.

options.label: C
options.text: Whomever happens upon the individual must promptly report the situation to a supervisor.

options.label: D
options.text: Only a manager who witnessed the incident directly can initiate the report.

questionsInjury.explanation: Section 3.1.2 states that if an employee is unable to report their own injury, whomever happens upon the individual must promptly report the situation to a supervisor.

questionsInjury.question: After administering first aid, what must the First Aid provider do?

options.label: A
options.text: Report only to the Board of Directors.

options.label: B
options.text: Wait 24 hours before logging anything.

options.label: C
options.text: Nothing further is required.

options.label: D
options.text: Record the treatment and advice given in the First Aid Log.

questionsInjury.explanation: Section 3.3.1 requires the First Aid provider to record given treatment and advice in the First Aid Log.

questionsInjury.question: How must an injury or illness initially be reported, per the Procedures section?

options.label: A
options.text: Immediately, verbally, and using the Injury/Illness Reporting Form.

options.label: B
options.text: Only through an anonymous hotline.

options.label: C
options.text: Only if a manager happens to be on-site at the time.

options.label: D
options.text: In writing only, within 48 hours.

questionsInjury.explanation: Section 4.1.1 states reporting must be done immediately, verbally, and using the Injury/Illness Reporting Form.

questionsMedia.question: A staff member who is not an authorized spokesperson is contacted directly by an external reporter for a quote. What should they do?

options.label: A
options.text: Provide the quote, since they know the subject well.

options.label: B
options.text: Decline to provide an attributable quote unless authorization has been received from the President or Senior Manager, Communications.

options.label: C
options.text: Refer the reporter to the Gazette instead.

options.label: D
options.text: Give a quote but ask to remain anonymous.

questionsMedia.explanation: Section 3.3.2 states management and staff are not authorized as spokespeople and shall not provide attributable quotes without authorization from the President or Senior Manager, Communications.

questionsMedia.question: A Vice-President wants a Coordinator within their own portfolio to speak to media on their behalf. Is this permitted?

options.label: A
options.text: Only for internal media outlets.

options.label: B
options.text: No, only the President can authorize this.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes — Vice-Presidents may authorize volunteers within their portfolio, such as Associates and Coordinators, to speak on their behalf.

options.label: D
options.text: Only with Board of Directors approval.

questionsMedia.explanation: Section 3.2.1.1 states Vice-Presidents may authorize volunteers within their portfolio to speak on their behalf.

questionsMedia.question: Which of the following is considered 'Internal Media' under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Any USC-run social media account.

options.label: B
options.text: Local London television news.

options.label: C
options.text: A national newspaper.

options.label: D
options.text: The Gazette, CHRW, Western News, or the Alumni Gazette.

questionsMedia.explanation: Section 2.1 defines Internal Media as the Gazette, CHRW, Western News, and the Alumni Gazette.

questionsMedia.question: A media matter falls outside the President's purview, such as a matter related to Elections. Who may the President authorize to speak on the organization's behalf?

options.label: A
options.text: The Senior Manager, Communications.

options.label: B
options.text: The Board of Directors Chairperson.

options.label: C
options.text: The Gazette editor.

options.label: D
options.text: Any available staff member.

questionsMedia.explanation: Section 3.3.1 states the President authorizes the Senior Manager, Communications to speak on behalf of the organization when a matter falls outside the President's purview.

questionsDisconnect.question: An employee feels pressure from their manager to respond to non-urgent emails late at night. What does the policy say they should do?

options.label: A
options.text: Simply comply to avoid conflict.

options.label: B
options.text: Notify their Manager or Supervisor that they feel pressure to respond outside normal hours.

options.label: C
options.text: Resign from the position.

options.label: D
options.text: Report it only to the Board of Directors.

questionsDisconnect.explanation: Section 5.3.3.6 directs employees to notify their Manager or Supervisor if they feel pressure to respond to issues outside of normal hours of work.

questionsDisconnect.question: An employee receives a cell phone stipend as part of their role. What does this mean for them under the policy's exceptions?

options.label: A
options.text: It only applies during declared emergencies.

options.label: B
options.text: It has no bearing on their disconnecting expectations.

options.label: C
options.text: They are required to stay in regular contact as per operational demand.

options.label: D
options.text: It means they are exempt from all normal hours of work.

questionsDisconnect.explanation: Section 5.2.2.8 lists cell phone stipend recipients as required to stay in regular contact as per operational demand.

questionsDisconnect.question: Will an employee face any penalty for complying with this Right to Disconnect procedure?

options.label: A
options.text: Only during a probationary period.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, unless pre-approved by a manager.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, if it affects team output.

options.label: D
options.text: No — employees will not be penalized or face reprisal for complying with the procedure.

questionsDisconnect.explanation: Section 5.1.3 states you will not be penalized or face reprisal for complying with this procedure.

questionsDisconnect.question: A new employee starts on September 1. By what deadline must People and Development provide them a copy of this procedure?

options.label: A
options.text: Within 30 days of their start date.

options.label: B
options.text: Within 90 days.

options.label: C
options.text: Within 7 days.

options.label: D
options.text: Within 14 days.

questionsDisconnect.explanation: Section 5.3.4.2 states People and Development will provide new employees with a copy of this procedure within 30 days of their start date.

questionsDisconnect.question: A manager takes reasonable corrective action after an employee repeatedly misses deadlines, shortly after the employee had asked questions about this policy. Does this corrective action count as reprisal?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, any corrective action following a policy question is automatically reprisal.

options.label: B
options.text: No — reasonable direction and corrective action are not considered reprisal.

options.label: C
options.text: Only if it is documented in writing.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, unless approved in advance by the Board.

questionsDisconnect.explanation: Section 5.3.2.7 states reasonable direction and corrective actions are not considered reprisal

questionsDisconnect.question: Which of the following is explicitly named as a mental health support resource associated with this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: A mandatory therapy program.

options.label: B
options.text: A quarterly wellness stipend.

options.label: C
options.text: LifeSpeak.

options.label: D
options.text: An external hotline unrelated to the USC.

questionsDisconnect.explanation: Section 5.5.1.4 names LifeSpeak, LifeWorks, and Wellness Wednesdays as examples of supportive resources.

questionsSocial.question: An employee wants to use AI-generated video content directly on an official USC social media account. Is this permitted?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, if approved by any coworker.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, without any restriction.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, as long as it looks professional.

options.label: D
options.text: No — AI-generated graphics, photos, or videos should not be used for official USC social media channels.

questionsSocial.explanation: Section 3.7 states AI-generated graphics, photos, or videos should not be used for official USC social media channels.

questionsSocial.question: A volunteer posts a comment about a USC policy on their personal social media account without identifying their USC relationship. What principle does this violate?

options.label: A
options.text: Transparency, which requires identifying a USC relationship and prohibits anonymous posting on USC topics.

options.label: B
options.text: Confidentiality.

options.label: C
options.text: Non-Discrimination.

options.label: D
options.text: Branding.

questionsSocial.explanation: Section 3.1 (Transparency) requires staff and volunteers to identify their relationship to the USC and states it is unacceptable to assume an anonymous identity on USC-related topics.

questionsSocial.question: Which platforms are specifically named as being contemplated by this policy, while its general principles still extend elsewhere?

options.label: A
options.text: LinkedIn, Snapchat, Pinterest, and Reddit.

options.label: B
options.text: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and X.

options.label: C
options.text: YouTube and Twitch only.

options.label: D
options.text: WhatsApp and Telegram.

questionsSocial.explanation: Section 2.3 states the policy specifically contemplates Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and X, while its general principles extend to other platforms.

questionsSocial.question: Who owns the content, followers, and materials associated with an official USC social media account?

options.label: A
options.text: Ownership transfers to the employee upon departure.

options.label: B
options.text: The employee or volunteer who created the account.

options.label: C
options.text: The USC — employees and volunteers have no ownership rights over these.

options.label: D
options.text: Jointly owned by the USC and the account's creator.

questionsSocial.explanation: Section 5.1 states USC social media accounts are property of the USC, and employees and volunteers have no ownership rights over content, followers, or other materials.

questionsSocial.question: A staff member wants to create a new official USC-related social media account. What must happen first?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the President can create new accounts personally.

options.label: B
options.text: It requires a resolution of the Board of Directors.

options.label: C
options.text: They can create it immediately without approval.

options.label: D
options.text: It must be created in consultation with the USC's Communications Department and ITS team.

questionsSocial.explanation: Section 5.3 states new USC-related social media accounts can only be created in consultation with the Communications Department and ITS team.

questionsVisitor.question: A visitor becomes ill while meeting with their USC host. What must happen?

options.label: A
options.text: The visitor and USC host must complete the Illness/Injury Reporting Form and submit it to the USC Health & Safety Coordinator.

options.label: B
options.text: Only the host needs to make a private, informal note of it.

options.label: C
options.text: It only needs to be reported if the visitor requests medical attention.

options.label: D
options.text: The visitor should simply leave without any report being made.

questionsVisitor.explanation: Section 4.4 requires the visitor and USC host to complete the Illness/Injury Reporting Form and submit it to the USC Health & Safety Coordinator.

questionsVisitor.question: A visitor repeatedly ignores directions from their USC host and refuses to follow USC procedures. What should the host do?

options.label: A
options.text: Continue the meeting and address it another time.

options.label: B
options.text: Ask the visitor to leave and report the incident to their manager.

options.label: C
options.text: Call Campus Police immediately, regardless of severity.

options.label: D
options.text: Simply end the meeting early, with no further action.

questionsVisitor.explanation: Section 4.5 directs the host to ask the visitor to leave and report the incident to their manager if the visitor refuses to follow USC procedures.

questionsVisitor.question: Once a visitor checks in, who is responsible for contacting the USC host to escort them?

options.label: A
options.text: Building Services.

options.label: B
options.text: The visitor must locate their host on their own.

options.label: C
options.text: The Executive Assistant or designate.

options.label: D
options.text: Any nearby employee.

questionsVisitor.explanation: Section 4.2 states the Executive Assistant or designate will contact the USC Host to escort the visitor to the designated meeting location.

questionsVisitor.question: Are visitors permitted to move freely around USC office spaces without an escort?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, if they have visited before.

options.label: B
options.text: Only in common areas.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, once they've checked in at reception.

options.label: D
options.text: No — visitors must always be escorted by their designated USC host while in USC spaces.

questionsVisitor.explanation: Section 3.1.2 requires visitors to always be escorted by their designated USC host while in USC spaces.

questionsWhistleblower.question: An employee wants to report suspected fraud but is worried about being identified. What does the policy say about confidentiality?

options.label: A
options.text: Violations or suspected violations may be submitted on a confidential basis, and will be kept confidential to the extent possible.

options.label: B
options.text: All complainants must be publicly named.

options.label: C
options.text: Confidentiality is only available to Board members.

options.label: D
options.text: Reports can never be made confidentially.

questionsWhistleblower.explanation: Sections 5.1 and 5.2 state violations may be submitted confidentially and will be kept confidential to the extent possible, consistent with conducting an adequate investigation.

questionsWhistleblower.question: A manager learns that an employee reported a suspected policy violation in good faith and begins treating them unfairly as a result. What is the consequence for the manager?

options.label: A
options.text: No consequence, since managers have full discretion.

options.label: B
options.text: The manager is subject to discipline up to and including termination.

options.label: C
options.text: Only a verbal reminder is given, regardless of severity.

options.label: D
options.text: The original complaint is simply dismissed.

questionsWhistleblower.explanation: Section 3.2 states an employee who retaliates against someone who has reported a violation in good faith is subject to discipline up to and including termination.

questionsWhistleblower.question: An employee wants to report a suspected violation involving general USC operations. Who should this typically be reported to?

options.label: A
options.text: External legal counsel only.

options.label: B
options.text: Directly to the Board of Directors in all cases.

options.label: C
options.text: The Chief Operating Officer.

options.label: D
options.text: The employee's own direct report only.

questionsWhistleblower.explanation: Section 6.1 states suspected violations of approved USC policy, fraud, or other misconduct should be reported to the Chief Operating Officer.

questionsWhistleblower.question: Someone knowingly files a completely baseless whistleblower complaint out of malice. How is this treated?

options.label: A
options.text: As protected activity, regardless of intent.

options.label: B
options.text: It cannot be addressed under this policy at all.

options.label: C
options.text: As a normal complaint requiring only a standard investigation.

options.label: D
options.text: As a serious disciplinary offense.

questionsWhistleblower.explanation: Section 4.2 states allegations that prove unsubstantiated and were made maliciously or knowingly false will be viewed as a serious disciplinary offense.

questionsWorkplace.question: A staff member makes a public comment that could be seen as compromising the USC's political impartiality. Does this policy address this?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes — Staff and volunteers must refrain from comments or actions that compromise the USC's political impartiality.

options.label: B
options.text: It's only restricted for Executive Members.

options.label: C
options.text: It's only restricted during election periods.

options.label: D
options.text: No, political commentary isn't addressed by this policy.

questionsWorkplace.explanation: Section 4.1 states Staff and volunteers shall refrain from making comments or performing actions that compromise the political impartiality of the USC.

questionsWorkplace.question: Two staff members are having a heated disagreement about a work process. What tone does the policy require they maintain?

options.label: A
options.text: Any tone is acceptable as long as the issue gets resolved.

options.label: B
options.text: A respectful tone and respectful language, regardless of the subject matter being discussed.

options.label: C
options.text: Formal written communication only, with no verbal discussion.

options.label: D
options.text: Silence until a manager is present to intervene.

questionsWorkplace.explanation: Section 3.2 requires individuals to maintain a respectful tone and use respectful language in all interpersonal interactions regardless of the subject matter.

questionsWorkplace.question: Who is responsible for establishing and amending further Procedures needed to implement this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: External legal counsel.

options.label: B
options.text: Any individual staff member, at their discretion.

options.label: C
options.text: The Human Resources Department, subject to ratification by the Board of Directors.

options.label: D
options.text: The Gazette.

questionsWorkplace.explanation: Sections 5.1 and 5.1.3 state Procedures are established and amended by Human Resources and must be ratified by the Board of Directors before taking effect.

questionsWorkplace.question: Does this policy apply to interactions at a USC-organized event held outside the Main Office space?

options.label: A
options.text: Only if a manager is present at the event.

options.label: B
options.text: Only for events lasting more than one day.

options.label: C
options.text: No, only conduct inside the Main Office is covered.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes — it applies to interactions of Staff and USC representatives at USC functions outside the Main Office space.

questionsWorkplace.explanation: Section 1.2 states this policy applies to interactions of Staff and USC representatives at USC functions outside of the USC Main Office space.

questionsWorkplace.question: An employee uses a colleague's belongings without permission in a shared workspace. What does the policy say?

options.label: A
options.text: Individuals shall respect the work spaces of others and refrain, wherever possible, from using others' belongings without permission.

options.label: B
options.text: This is only an issue if the item is damaged.

options.label: C
options.text: Shared workspaces have no expectations around personal belongings.

options.label: D
options.text: This is acceptable as long as the items are returned.

questionsWorkplace.explanation: Section 4.4 states individuals shall respect the work spaces of others and refrain, wherever possible, from using others' belongings without permission, explicit or otherwise.

questionsDisc2.question: A complainant wants to file a formal written complaint about an incident that occurred 14 months ago. What does the procedure say?

options.label: A
options.text: Complaints can only be filed within 30 days of an incident.

options.label: B
options.text: Only verbal complaints are accepted after six months.

options.label: C
options.text: It must be accepted and investigated regardless of timing.

options.label: D
options.text: The Corporation reserves the right not to pursue a complaint filed more than 12 months after the last incident.

questionsDisc2.explanation: Section 5.1.1 states the Corporation reserves the right not to pursue a complaint filed more than 12 months after the last incident or event of alleged harassment.

questionsDisc2.question: An investigation into a complaint has just concluded, with a written report of findings completed. Within how many calendar days must the complainant receive a summary of the findings and corrective action?

options.label: A
options.text: 10 calendar days.

options.label: B
options.text: 30 calendar days.

options.label: C
options.text: 90 calendar days.

options.label: D
options.text: 5 calendar days.

questionsDisc2.explanation: Step Four(g) of the Investigations Procedure states the summary of findings and corrective action will be provided to the Complainant within 10 calendar days of the investigation being concluded.

questionsDisc2.question: An investigation finds the evidence does not support the allegation, but the complaint was filed honestly and in good faith. What happens to the complainant?

options.label: A
options.text: They are disciplined for filing an unfounded complaint.

options.label: B
options.text: No penalty is applied and no record is placed in the Respondent's file.

options.label: C
options.text: They are required to publicly retract the complaint.

options.label: D
options.text: Their identity is automatically disclosed to the Respondent's department.

questionsDisc2.explanation: Step Five(f) and Section 5.6 state that if a good-faith complaint isn't supported by evidence, it is dismissed with no record placed in the Respondent's file and no penalty to the complainant.

questionsDisc2.question: An employee deliberately and maliciously files a complaint they know has no basis. What is the likely consequence?

options.label: A
options.text: The complaint is simply set aside with no further action.

options.label: B
options.text: No consequence, since all complaints are protected.

options.label: C
options.text: The complainant will be disciplined similarly to someone who violated the Prevention Policy.

options.label: D
options.text: Only a verbal reminder regardless of severity.

questionsDisc2.explanation: Step Five(h) states that a complaint made in bad faith results in discipline for the complainant, with penalties the same as for discrimination or harassment.

questionsDisc2.question: Within what maximum timeframe should a formal investigation normally be completed, absent extenuating circumstances?

options.label: A
options.text: 120 calendar days.

options.label: B
options.text: 30 calendar days.

options.label: C
options.text: 60 calendar days.

options.label: D
options.text: 90 calendar days.

questionsDisc2.explanation: Step Four(e) states investigations will be completed within 90 calendar days unless extenuating circumstances warrant a longer investigation.

questionsDisc2.question: If the Chief Operating Officer is the Respondent in a complaint, who is notified to administer the procedure?

options.label: A
options.text: The USC President, who consults with the Board of Directors.

options.label: B
options.text: An external investigator is automatically appointed with no internal notification.

options.label: C
options.text: The complaint is automatically dismissed.

options.label: D
options.text: The Senior Manager, People and Development handles it alone.

questionsDisc2.explanation: Section 2.2 states that if the COO is the Respondent, the Senior Manager, People and Development shall notify the USC President, who shall administer the Procedure in consultation with the Board.

questionsDisc2.question: A colleague retaliates against a coworker after learning they gave evidence in a harassment investigation. How is this treated under the procedure?

options.label: A
options.text: As a minor issue requiring only a verbal reminder.

options.label: B
options.text: As a serious disciplinary breach, with penalties the same as those for a substantiated policy violation.

options.label: C
options.text: It is only addressed if the original complaint was substantiated.

options.label: D
options.text: Only Human Resources is informed; no discipline applies.

questionsDisc2.explanation: Section 5.6.1 states retaliation is considered a serious disciplinary breach, with possible penalties the same as those assessed for a contravention of the Prevention Policy.

questionsDisc2.question: An employee believes a coworker's ongoing comments are unwelcome, but the nature of the relationship makes it unsafe to address it directly. What should they do?

options.label: A
options.text: Handle it entirely through informal peer mediation with no involvement from People and Development.

options.label: B
options.text: Say nothing, since direct confrontation is always required first.

options.label: C
options.text: Bring the matter to the attention of the Senior Manager, People and Development.

options.label: D
options.text: Wait for the behaviour to escalate further before reporting.

questionsDisc2.explanation: Section 3.2.1 states that if it is unreasonable or unsafe to address the behaviour directly, the individual is responsible for bringing the matter to the Senior Manager, People and Development.

questionsProf.question: A staff member wants to take a course on a hobby that is interesting but unrelated to a performance concern, a job requirement, or new technology/skill development. What does the policy suggest?

options.label: A
options.text: Book it and submit for reimbursement afterward.

options.label: B
options.text: Consider using their personal courses benefit.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask the Board of Directors to approve it as an exception.

options.label: D
options.text: Charge it to a corporate credit card and repay it later.

questionsProf.explanation: Section 2.2 states that learning opportunities outside the approved purposes should be pursued through the personal courses benefit.

questionsProf.question: A coordinator registers for and pays for a conference with a corporate credit card, planning to ask for approval once they return. What is the likely outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The conference is reimbursed automatically since it was work-related.

options.label: B
options.text: Approval can be granted retroactively with no consequence.

options.label: C
options.text: Only half of the cost is reimbursed.

options.label: D
options.text: It will not be reimbursed, and the employee may be required to pay back the amount charged to the credit card.

questionsProf.explanation: Section 3.1 requires approval prior to booking, and section 3.1.1 states unapproved events will not be reimbursed and may have to be paid back if charged to a corporate credit card.

questionsProf.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the purposes for which professional development will be considered under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Addressing a specific performance concern.

options.label: B
options.text: Fulfilling a job requirement.

options.label: C
options.text: Pursuing a personal interest unrelated to the employee's role.

options.label: D
options.text: Learning about new technology or developing skills.

questionsProf.explanation: Section 2.1 lists three purposes: a specific performance concern, a job requirement, and new technology or skill development. Unrelated personal interests fall outside the policy.

questionsProf.question: An Executive wants to attend a leadership training session as part of their development. What does the policy require?

options.label: A
options.text: Executive professional development must be pre-approved, following the Professional Development Procedure.

options.label: B
options.text: Executives are exempt from the approval requirement.

options.label: C
options.text: Approval is only needed if the cost exceeds a set amount.

options.label: D
options.text: Approval can be requested after attending.

questionsProf.explanation: Sections 4.2 and 4.3 state all Executive professional development must be pre-approved, with approval details in the Professional Development Procedure.
